ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=10\text{cm}$, $DE$ is a perpendicular bisector of $AB$ with the foot of the perpendicular being at $E$, and it intersects $AC$ at $D$. If the perimeter of $\triangle DBC$ is $18\text{cm}$, what is the length of $BC$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the perimeter of $\triangle DBC$ equals BC + BD + CD $= 18\,\text{cm}$,\\
and since DE perpendicularly bisects AB,\\
thus AD $=$ BD,\\
hence BC + AD + CD $= 18\,\text{cm}$,\\
since AC $=$ AD + DC $= 10\,\text{cm}$,\\
therefore BC $= 18 - 10 = \boxed{8}\,\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is on side AC; point E is on side AB; line DE passes through E and D, and is perpendicular to AB at E, marked in the figure with a right-angle symbol. The figure also shows line segment BD connecting B and D. Then reason: it is known that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AB, therefore point D on DE has equal distances to points A and B, so DB = DA. The perimeter of triangle DBC is BD + DC + BC = 18. Substitute using BD = DA, obtaining DA + DC + BC = 18. Because D is on AC, DA + DC = AC = 10. Thus 10 + BC = 18, obtaining BC = 8 cm.
